item.text: After three days, X reports four installs: three from the “£0 to download” post and one from the QR post, on roughly equal spend. I’ll shift more budget to the free-download post while keeping the QR post running for comparison. The sample is still small.

Through 2 July, the campaign has spent $182.57 and reported seven installs. The free-download post still leads at about $23 per install, versus $34 for the QR post. I’ve also narrowed the smaller QR ad group to market-related phrases to test whether a more relevant audience improves its results.

item.text: With four days left, X reports nine installs on $274.44 spent. I’ve added your approved 9 July reminder to the larger ad group for the closing stretch. The campaign remains capped at $400.

The recent results favour the market-focused ad group: three installs from $29.51 since 4 July, compared with two from $93.93 in the broader group. I’ll move $20 of the remaining budget to it for the final two days, keeping the combined cap at $400.
The 13-day flight has ended, and I’ve paused the campaign. I’m checking the final spend, delivery and install totals for your recap.

The campaign ran 27 June–9 July inclusive, UK time, and is now paused.

| Result | Total |
|---|---:|
| Spend | $398.97 USD |
| Impressions | 368,581 |
| Link clicks | 187 |
| “Wallet installed” installs | 15 |
| Cost per install | $26.60 |

The “£0 to download” post led early, so I increased its budget. Later, the market-focused audience delivered cheaper installs, so I shifted remaining budget towards it.

X attributed 11 installs after engagement and four after viewing. These are the totals currently reported; delayed attribution may update them.
